n−12​fBackBone=xr.i.0n12+𝒪⁡(log⁡nn12)n^{-\frac{1}{2}}f_{\text{BackBone}}=\frac{x^{0}_{r.i.}}{n^{\frac{1}{2}}}+{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{n^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) (94)

where xr.i.0x^{0}_{r.i.} denote the random initialized version of fBackBonef_{\text{BackBone}}.

NTK w.r.t. fBackBonef_{\text{BackBone}} is

1n​W​JBackBone​(θPT)​JBackBone⊤​(θPT)​W⊤\frac{1}{n}WJ_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{\text{PT}})J^{\top}_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{\text{PT}})W^{\top} (95)

For JBackBone​(θPT)J_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{\text{PT}}), we have

JBackBone​(θ0)+ΔJ_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{0})+\Delta (96)

where θ0\theta_{0} is the random initialization when training fPTf_{\text{PT}}, and Δ\Delta is the differece between these two, i.e., JBackBone​(θPT)−JBackBone​(θ0)J_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{\text{PT}})-J_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{0}). This term can also be controlled by 𝒪⁡(log⁡nn12){\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{n^{\frac{1}{2}}}\right) using because of the local lipschtiz result we proved above. Putting these all together, the NTK here becomes

1n​W​JBackBone​(θ0)​JBackBone⊤​(θ0)​W⊤+xr.i.0​xr.i.0⊤n+e\frac{1}{n}WJ_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{0})J^{\top}_{\text{BackBone}}(\theta_{0})W^{\top}+\frac{x^{0}_{r.i.}{x^{0}_{r.i.}}^{\top}}{n}+e (97)

B.5 Main results

Based on the the Local Lipschitzness property proved above, we can get the following NTK convergence results under the two types of fine-tuning settings.

(98)

and

supτ‖K0−Kτ‖F≤6​L3​R0N22​λmin​n−12\sup_{\tau}\left\|K_{0}-K_{\tau}\right\|_{F}\leq\frac{6L^{3}R_{0}}{{N_{2}}^{2}\lambda_{\min}}n^{-\frac{1}{2}} (99)

where K0K_{0} is the empirical kernel matrix induced by fPTf_{\text{PT}} and KτK_{\tau} is the one induced by fτf_{\tau} using target data 𝐗tgt\bm{X}^{\text{tgt}}.

Under assumptions 4.1 - 4.7 in the main text, we are able to linearize the fine-tuned network fPTf_{\text{PT}} around the pretrained model fPTf_{\text{PT}}, i.e., we have

fFT\displaystyle f_{\text{FT}} =fPT+Δθ∇fPT(θ)+e\displaystyle=f_{\text{PT}}+\Delta\theta\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta)+e (100)
=fPT+∑iζi​𝕂​(⋅,𝐗i)+e\displaystyle=f_{\text{PT}}+\sum_{i}\zeta_{i}\mathbb{K}(\cdot,\mathbf{X}_{i})+e

For any γ>0\gamma>0, there exists M∈ℕM\in\mathbb{N}, a full connected neural network with width and hidden dimension n≥Mn\geq M, the following holds with probability at least 1−γ−c1​exp⁡(−c2​N​ϱ^N2)1-\gamma-c_{1}\exp\left(-c_{2}N\widehat{\varrho}_{N}^{2}\right) over pre-trained initialization when applying gradient descent with learning rate ϵ=η0m\epsilon=\frac{\eta_{0}}{m}, and η0\eta_{0} for standard parameterization and NTK parameterization, respectively

Appendix C Task Arithmetic

C.1 Proof of Corollary 5.1.1

Apply Lemma 6, consider the operation of negating a task vector τ\tau, for the resulting network and fFTf_{\text{FT}}, we have

fneg=fPT−τ∇fPT(θ)+e1,fFT≈fPT+τ∇fPT(θ)+e2f_{\text{neg}}=f_{\text{PT}}-\tau\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta)+e_{1},\quad f_{\text{FT}}\approx f_{\text{PT}}+\tau\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta)+e_{2} (103)

Consider evaluate fnegf_{\text{neg}} and fFTf_{\text{FT}} on test sets using the MSE loss. We can compute M​S​E​(fneg)−M​S​E​(fFT)MSE(f_{\text{neg}})-MSE(f_{\text{FT}}):

4(Ytest−fPT(Xtest))⊤τ∇fPT(θ,Xtest).4\left(Y^{\text{test}}-f_{\text{PT}}(X^{\text{test}})\right)^{\top}\tau\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta,X^{\text{test}}). (104)

Then apply Theorem 7, we can approximate YtestY^{\text{test}} as

Ytest=fPT(Xtest)+τ∇fPT(θ,Xtest)+wtest+e3Y^{\text{test}}=f_{\text{PT}}(X^{\text{test}})+\tau\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta,X^{\text{test}})+w^{\text{test}}+e_{3} (105)

Then the expectation of the above difference, we have

𝔼[MSE(fneg)−MSE(fFT)]=𝔼[4∇fPT(θ,Xtest)⊤τ⊤τ∇fPT(θ,Xtest)]+∑i=13𝔼ei\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[MSE(f_{\text{neg}})-MSE(f_{\text{FT}})\right]=\mathbb{E}\left[4{\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta,X^{\text{test}})}^{\top}\tau^{\top}\tau\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta,X^{\text{test}})\right]+\sum_{i=1}^{3}\mathbb{E}e_{i} (106)

Since the error of eie_{i} can be controlled by 𝒪~​(1n1/2)\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{1}{{n}^{1/2}}\right) with sufficiently large width and ∇fPT​(θ,Xtest){\nabla f_{\text{PT}}(\theta,X^{\text{test}})} converges to some stationary Jacobian in probability, we can conclude that w.h.p. 𝔼⁡[M​S​E​(fneg)−M​S​E​(fFT)]>0\mathbb{E}\left[MSE(f_{\text{neg}})-MSE(f_{\text{FT}})\right]>0 when the width and hidden dimension nn is sufficiently large.

C.2 Proof of Corollary 5.1.2

For the corresponding fine-tuning model, apply Lemma 6, we have

fFT1\displaystyle f_{\text{FT}_{1}} =fPT+∑𝐗i∈𝑿task1γit​𝕂​(⋅,𝐗i)⏟g1+e1\displaystyle=f_{\text{PT}}+\underbrace{\sum_{\mathbf{X}_{i}\in\bm{X}^{\text{task}_{1}}}\gamma^{t}_{i}\mathbb{K}(\cdot,\mathbf{X}_{i})}_{g_{1}}+e_{1} (107)

And this indicates the multi task model obtained by applying task vector can be written as

𝕂⁡(𝐗i,𝐗j)=0.\mathbb{K}(\mathbf{X}_{i},\mathbf{X}_{j})=0. (109)
